The Foxmen are a cult of Tali, God of the Wind. He has no formal priesthood but many shrines built in the most remote and dangerous parts of Erebus. Some say the Foxmen put them there just to give each other excuses to travel. The Foxmen are renowned for their Wanderlust. They cannot stand to stay still for very long. There are no better explorers than their Drifters, nor better story tellers. The closest thing to a mass religious service are the convocations that they Foxmen are known to hold on the rooftops of popular inns, where they regale each other with tall tales of their past or future exploits. It weakened by [LINK=IMPROVEMENT_IMPROVEMENT_CAGE]Cages[\LINK], [LINK=BONUS_MANA_EARTH]Earth Mana[\LINK], and by having fortified too long in one place.

[TAB]Mages spent weeks in meditation, exploring the farthest reaches of the ethereal world. The demands of the body were ignored, and they survived sustained only by magic. Their efforts were rewarded, a sentience was contacted, dark and horrible. It whispered secrets into the mages' minds, secrets of necromancy, diseases, and sacrificial rites. It promised power in exchange for their blood, and they freely gave it. Deep with the richest areas of the world (and only those areas) great temples to Amathaon provide rest and an endless bounty to those that would join them. They are less about worship and more about providing hospitality, like the world's best bed and breakfast.
